summary: Byte-push writer over an allocator-managed buffer descriptor a2 (current position, element count, allocation end, flag word). Rejects the sentinel input a1 == -1 and flag-state mismatches, lazily initializes the descriptor via MemoryAllocatorInit when no allocation exists, then either writes byte a1 at a decremented position or verifies it matches in match mode (flag 0x40). Returns the byte on success, -1 on failure.

operations.description: Reject the sentinel input: return -1 immediately when a1 == -1.
Read the flag word a2[3]; return -1 when bit 0x1 is clear and (bit 0x80 is clear or bit 0x2 is set), i.e. the descriptor is not in a writable state.
Lazily initialize the descriptor: when the allocation pointer a2[2] is null, call MemoryAllocatorInit(a2).
When the current position *a2 equals the allocation end a2[2]: reject if the element count a2[1] is nonzero, otherwise advance the current position.
Match mode (flag 0x40 set): decrement the current position and compare the stored byte against a1; on mismatch restore the position and return -1.
Write mode (flag 0x40 clear): decrement the current position and store byte a1 there.
Bump the element count a2[1] and update the flag word: a2[3] = (a2[3] & 0xEE) | 1.
Return the written/verified byte as an unsigned char of a1.

unresolved: The concrete class of descriptor a2 is unproven; MemoryAllocatorInit on it only proves it is allocator-managed.
The semantics of the flag bits (0x1, 0x2, 0x40, 0x80) beyond the observed transitions are unproven.
Whether a2[1] counts bytes or elements is undetermined.
